    }

Step 2: Update character.gd to show combat feedback

Update apply_state() in roguelite/scripts/entities/character.gd:

extends Node2D
## Visual representation of a simulation entity (player or enemy).
## No physics — position set directly from snapshots.

@onready var sprite: Sprite2D = $Sprite
@onready var name_label: Label = $NameLabel
@onready var hp_bar: ProgressBar = $HPBar

var entity_id: String = ""
var entity_type: int = 0  # EntityType enum value


func setup(id: String, type_val: int, display_name: String = "") -> void:
    entity_id = id
    entity_type = type_val
    name_label.text = display_name if display_name != "" else id

    # Color by type: blue = player, red = melee enemy, orange = ranged, yellow = projectile.
    match type_val:
        1:  # PLAYER
            sprite.modulate = Color.CORNFLOWER_BLUE
        2:  # ENEMY_MELEE
            sprite.modulate = Color.INDIAN_RED
        3:  # ENEMY_RANGED
            sprite.modulate = Color.ORANGE
        4:  # PROJECTILE
            sprite.modulate = Color.YELLOW
            sprite.scale = Vector2(0.4, 0.4)
            name_label.visible = false
            hp_bar.visible = false
        _:
            sprite.modulate = Color.WHITE


func apply_state(state: Dictionary) -> void:
    # Position from snapshot.
    position = Vector2(state.get("x", 0.0), state.get("y", 0.0))

    # Projectiles: just update position, no HP bar.
    if entity_type == 4:  # PROJECTILE
        return

    # HP bar.
    var hp: float = state.get("health", 0)
    var max_hp: float = state.get("maxHealth", 1)
    hp_bar.value = hp / max_hp * 100.0
    hp_bar.visible = hp > 0

    # Action feedback.
    var action: int = int(state.get("action", 0))
    match action:
        4:  # ACTION_DEAD
            modulate.a = 0.3
            hp_bar.visible = false
        2:  # ACTION_ATTACK
            sprite.modulate.a = 1.0
            sprite.scale = Vector2(1.3, 1.3)
        _:
            modulate.a = 1.0
            sprite.scale = Vector2(1.0, 1.0)

Step 3: Update _spawn_entities to handle new entity types appearing mid-playback

In roguelite/scripts/main.gd, update _on_playback_tick() to handle projectiles spawning mid-simulation:

func _on_playback_tick(_tick_index: int, snapshot: Dictionary) -> void:
    var entity_states: Array = snapshot.get("entities", [])

    # Track which entities are in this snapshot.
    var seen_ids: Dictionary = {}
    for state: Dictionary in entity_states:
        var eid: String = state.get("id", "")
        seen_ids[eid] = true

        if eid in _entities:
            _entities[eid].apply_state(state)
        else:
            # New entity (e.g. projectile spawned mid-sim).
            var etype: int = int(state.get("type", 0))
            var character: Node2D = CharacterScene.instantiate()
            entities_node.add_child(character)
            character.setup(eid, etype)
            character.apply_state(state)
            _entities[eid] = character

    # Remove entities no longer in snapshot (e.g. destroyed projectiles).
    var to_remove: Array = []
    for eid: String in _entities:
        if eid not in seen_ids:
            _entities[eid].queue_free()
            to_remove.append(eid)
    for eid: String in to_remove:
        _entities.erase(eid)

docs.title: Notes for Implementer
docs.text:
• Backward compatibility is paramount. Every task must keep existing tests passing. nil skills = basic_attack only. nil stats = use EntityConfig fields directly. Zero-valued new proto fields = no behavior change.
  • Deterministic RNG. rand.New(rand.NewSource(42)) is created once per Simulate() call and passed to all functions that need randomness. NEVER use math/rand global functions.
  • Proto field numbering. New fields are added at the end of existing messages. Never reuse or reorder field numbers.
  • Proto enum string serialization. GDScript client sends proto enums as strings ("DAMAGE_PHYSICAL", "SHAPE_MELEE"). Server uses protojson which handles this automatically.
  • Projectile ownership. Projectiles store a pointer to their owner entity for damage calculation. The owner's stats at time of firing are used (not current stats). This is intentional.
  • Enemy AI uses PlayerBuild. Enemy templates generate a *pb.PlayerBuild with GlobalAi set. This reuses the same BuildExecutor() path as players. No special-casing.
  • Default AI tree doesn't select skills by name. The default UseSkill{} node (no SkillName, no Tags) falls back to basic_attack behavior. Only blueprints with explicit skill/tags parameters trigger skill selection. This means enemies with shoot_arrow need their AI tree to specify {"skill": "shoot_arrow"} in the UseSkill node parameters.
  • calcDamageV2 order of operations: dodge → block → skill mult → armor/resistance → crit → floor at 1. This matches the GDD specification.
  • Imports to add: "math/rand" in simulator.go, "strings" in builder.go, "fmt" and "math" in enemies.go.

docs.title: Phase 4a: UI Foundation — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For Claude: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

Goal: Full in-game UI system — main menu, settings, character profile, blueprint editor with GraphEdit, all integrated into the game loop.

Architecture: All screens are fullscreen Control nodes managed by UIManager autoload (show/hide + navigation stack). Blueprint editor uses Godot GraphEdit for visual AI tree building, serializes to PlayerBuild Dictionary matching protojson format. Dark theme applied globally via Project Settings.

Tech Stack: Godot 4.6 (GDScript), GraphEdit/GraphNode, ConfigFile for settings, Theme resource for styling.

Step 1: Create UIManager

# roguelite/scripts/autoload/ui_manager.gd
extends Node
## Screen navigation manager (autoload singleton).
## Manages fullscreen UI screens with history stack for Back navigation.

signal screen_changed(screen_name: String)

var _screens: Dictionary = {}  # name → Control node
var _history: Array[String] = []
var _current: String = ""


func register_screen(screen_name: String, node: Control) -> void:
    _screens[screen_name] = node
    node.visible = false


func navigate_to(screen_name: String) -> void:
    if screen_name == _current:
        return
    if not _screens.has(screen_name):
        push_error("UIManager: unknown screen '%s'" % screen_name)
        return

    if _current != "":
        _history.push_back(_current)

    _current = screen_name
    _apply()
    screen_changed.emit(screen_name)


func go_back() -> bool:
    if _history.is_empty():
        return false
    _current = _history.pop_back()
    _apply()
    screen_changed.emit(_current)
    return true


func clear_history() -> void:
    _history.clear()


func get_current() -> String:
    return _current


func _apply() -> void:
    for name: String in _screens:
        _screens[name].visible = (name == _current)


func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
    if event.is_action_pressed("ui_cancel"):
        if go_back():
            get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()

# roguelite/scripts/autoload/settings_manager.gd
extends Node
## Settings persistence via ConfigFile (autoload singleton).
## Saved to user://settings.cfg.

const SETTINGS_PATH := "user://settings.cfg"

# Video
var window_mode: int = DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED:
    set(v):
        window_mode = v
        DisplayServer.window_set_mode(v)
        _save()

var vsync: bool = true:
    set(v):
        vsync = v
        DisplayServer.window_set_vsync_mode(
            DisplayServer.VSYNC_ENABLED if v else DisplayServer.VSYNC_DISABLED
        )
        _save()

var screen_shake: bool = true:
    set(v):
        screen_shake = v
        _save()

# Audio
var master_volume: float = 1.0:
    set(v):
        master_volume = clampf(v, 0.0, 1.0)
        AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(0, linear_to_db(master_volume))
        _save()

var music_volume: float = 0.8:
    set(v):
        music_volume = clampf(v, 0.0, 1.0)
        var idx := AudioServer.get_bus_index("Music")
        if idx >= 0:
            AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(idx, linear_to_db(music_volume))
        _save()

var sfx_volume: float = 1.0:
    set(v):
        sfx_volume = clampf(v, 0.0, 1.0)
        var idx := AudioServer.get_bus_index("SFX")
        if idx >= 0:
            AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(idx, linear_to_db(sfx_volume))
        _save()

# Gameplay
var default_playback_speed: float = 1.0:
    set(v):
        default_playback_speed = clampf(v, 0.5, 4.0)
        _save()

var show_ai_decisions: bool = false:
    set(v):
        show_ai_decisions = v
        _save()


func _ready() -> void:
    _load()


func _load() -> void:
    var cfg := ConfigFile.new()
    if cfg.load(SETTINGS_PATH) != OK:
        return  # First launch, use defaults

    window_mode = cfg.get_value("video", "window_mode", DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED)
    vsync = cfg.get_value("video", "vsync", true)
    screen_shake = cfg.get_value("video", "screen_shake", true)
    master_volume = cfg.get_value("audio", "master_volume", 1.0)
    music_volume = cfg.get_value("audio", "music_volume", 0.8)
    sfx_volume = cfg.get_value("audio", "sfx_volume", 1.0)
    default_playback_speed = cfg.get_value("gameplay", "default_playback_speed", 1.0)
    show_ai_decisions = cfg.get_value("gameplay", "show_ai_decisions", false)


func _save() -> void:
    var cfg := ConfigFile.new()
    cfg.set_value("video", "window_mode", window_mode)
    cfg.set_value("video", "vsync", vsync)
    cfg.set_value("video", "screen_shake", screen_shake)
    cfg.set_value("audio", "master_volume", master_volume)
    cfg.set_value("audio", "music_volume", music_volume)
    cfg.set_value("audio", "sfx_volume", sfx_volume)
    cfg.set_value("gameplay", "default_playback_speed", default_playback_speed)
    cfg.set_value("gameplay", "show_ai_decisions", show_ai_decisions)
    cfg.save(SETTINGS_PATH)

# roguelite/scripts/ui/settings_screen.gd
extends Control
## Settings screen with Video, Audio, Gameplay tabs.

@onready var tabs: TabContainer = $VBox/TabContainer
@onready var back_btn: Button = $VBox/BackButton

# Video
@onready var window_mode_btn: OptionButton = $VBox/TabContainer/Video/WindowMode/OptionButton

# Audio

@onready var music_slider: HSlider = $VBox/TabContainer/Audio/Music/HSlider
@onready var sfx_slider: HSlider = $VBox/TabContainer/Audio/SFX/HSlider

# Gameplay
@onready var speed_btn: OptionButton = $VBox/TabContainer/Gameplay/PlaybackSpeed/OptionButton


func _ready() -> void:
    UIManager.register_screen("settings", self)
    back_btn.pressed.connect(func(): UIManager.go_back())

    # Populate window mode options.
    window_mode_btn.add_item("Windowed", 0)
    window_mode_btn.add_item("Fullscreen", 1)
    window_mode_btn.add_item("Borderless Fullscreen", 2)

    # Populate playback speed options.
    speed_btn.add_item("0.5x", 0)
    speed_btn.add_item("1x", 1)
    speed_btn.add_item("2x", 2)
    speed_btn.add_item("4x", 3)

    _load_current()

    # Connect signals.
    window_mode_btn.item_selected.connect(_on_window_mode)
    vsync_check.toggled.connect(func(v: bool): SettingsManager.vsync = v)
    master_slider.value_changed.connect(func(v: float): SettingsManager.master_volume = v)
    music_slider.value_changed.connect(func(v: float): SettingsManager.music_volume = v)
    sfx_slider.value_changed.connect(func(v: float): SettingsManager.sfx_volume = v)
    speed_btn.item_selected.connect(_on_speed)


func _load_current() -> void:
    # Map DisplayServer window mode to OptionButton index.
    match SettingsManager.window_mode:
        DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED:
            window_mode_btn.selected = 0
        DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN:
            window_mode_btn.selected = 1
        DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_EXCLUSIVE_FULLSCREEN:
            window_mode_btn.selected = 2
        _:
            window_mode_btn.selected = 0

    vsync_check.button_pressed = SettingsManager.vsync

    master_slider.value = SettingsManager.master_volume
    music_slider.value = SettingsManager.music_volume
    sfx_slider.value = SettingsManager.sfx_volume

    # Map speed to index.
    var speed_map := {0.5: 0, 1.0: 1, 2.0: 2, 4.0: 3}
    speed_btn.selected = speed_map.get(SettingsManager.default_playback_speed, 1)


func _on_window_mode(idx: int) -> void:
    match idx:
        0: SettingsManager.window_mode = DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED
        1: SettingsManager.window_mode = DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN
        2: SettingsManager.window_mode = DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_EXCLUSIVE_FULLSCREEN


func _on_speed(idx: int) -> void:
    var speeds := [0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0]
    if idx >= 0 and idx < speeds.size():
        SettingsManager.default_playback_speed = speeds[idx]

Step 1: Create game_view.gd

Extract the playback logic from main.gd into a standalone screen:

# roguelite/scripts/game_view.gd
extends Control
## Game view screen — handles server connection, simulation playback, results.

const CharacterScene := preload("res://scenes/entities/character.tscn")

@onready var viewport_container: SubViewportContainer = $SubViewportContainer
@onready var sub_viewport: SubViewport = $SubViewportContainer/SubViewport
@onready var entities_node: Node2D = $SubViewportContainer/SubViewport/World/Entities
@onready var camera: Camera2D = $SubViewportContainer/SubViewport/World/Camera2D
@onready var status_label: Label = $StatusLabel
@onready var result_panel: PanelContainer = $ResultPanel
@onready var result_label: Label = $ResultPanel/VBox/ResultLabel
@onready var continue_btn: Button = $ResultPanel/VBox/ContinueButton

var _entities: Dictionary = {}  # entity_id → Character node
var _build: Dictionary = {}


func _ready() -> void:
    UIManager.register_screen("game_view", self)
    NetworkManager.connected.connect(_on_connected)
    NetworkManager.disconnected.connect(_on_disconnected)
    NetworkManager.join_response_received.connect(_on_join_response)
    NetworkManager.simulation_result_received.connect(_on_simulation_result)
    NetworkManager.error_received.connect(_on_error)
    PlaybackManager.playback_tick.connect(_on_playback_tick)
    PlaybackManager.playback_finished.connect(_on_playback_finished)
    continue_btn.pressed.connect(_on_continue)
    result_panel.visible = false


func start_run(build: Dictionary) -> void:
    _build = build
    result_panel.visible = false
    _set_status("Connecting to server...")
    GameManager.change_state(GameManager.GameState.CONNECTING)
    NetworkManager.connect_to_server()


func _on_connected() -> void:
    _set_status("Connected. Joining room...")
    NetworkManager.send_join("Player")


func _on_disconnected() -> void:
    _set_status("Disconnected from server.")


func _on_join_response(data: Dictionary) -> void:
    if not data.get("success", false):
        _set_status("Join failed: %s" % data.get("error", "unknown"))
        return

    GameManager.player_id = data.get("playerId", "")
    GameManager.room_id = data.get("roomId", "")
    GameManager.change_state(GameManager.GameState.UPLOADING)

    _set_status("Uploading build...")
    NetworkManager.send_upload_build(_build)
    NetworkManager.send_ready()
    GameManager.change_state(GameManager.GameState.WAITING_SIM)
    _set_status("Simulating...")


func _on_simulation_result(data: Dictionary) -> void:
    GameManager.change_state(GameManager.GameState.PLAYBACK)
    PlaybackManager.load_result(data)

    var snapshots: Array = data.get("snapshots", [])
    if snapshots.is_empty():
        _set_status("Empty simulation!")
        return

    _spawn_entities(snapshots[0])
    _set_status("Playback — %d ticks" % snapshots.size())
    PlaybackManager.set_speed(SettingsManager.default_playback_speed)
    PlaybackManager.play()


func _on_playback_tick(_tick_index: int, snapshot: Dictionary) -> void:
    var entity_states: Array = snapshot.get("entities", [])
    var seen_ids: Dictionary = {}

    for state: Dictionary in entity_states:
        var eid: String = state.get("id", "")
        seen_ids[eid] = true
        if eid in _entities:
            _entities[eid].apply_state(state)
        else:
            var etype: int = int(state.get("type", 0))
            var character: Node2D = CharacterScene.instantiate()
            entities_node.add_child(character)
            character.setup(eid, etype)
            character.apply_state(state)
            _entities[eid] = character

    var to_remove: Array = []
    for eid: String in _entities:
        if eid not in seen_ids:
            _entities[eid].queue_free()
            to_remove.append(eid)
    for eid: String in to_remove:
        _entities.erase(eid)


func _on_playback_finished() -> void:
    var victory: bool = PlaybackManager.victory
    result_label.text = "ПОБЕДА!" if victory else "ПОРАЖЕНИЕ"
    result_panel.visible = true
    continue_btn.grab_focus()
    GameManager.change_state(GameManager.GameState.GAME_OVER)


func _on_continue() -> void:
    _cleanup()
    UIManager.navigate_to("profile")


func _on_error(message: String) -> void:
    _set_status("Error: %s" % message)


func _spawn_entities(first_snapshot: Dictionary) -> void:
    _cleanup()
    for state: Dictionary in first_snapshot.get("entities", []):
        var eid: String = state.get("id", "")
        var etype: int = int(state.get("type", 0))
        var character: Node2D = CharacterScene.instantiate()
        entities_node.add_child(character)
        character.setup(eid, etype)
        character.apply_state(state)
        _entities[eid] = character


func _cleanup() -> void:
    for child in entities_node.get_children():
        child.queue_free()
    _entities.clear()


func _set_status(text: String) -> void:
    status_label.text = text


func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
    if not visible:
        return
    if event is InputEventKey and event.pressed:
        match event.keycode:
            KEY_SPACE:
                if PlaybackManager.is_playing:
                    PlaybackManager.pause()
                    _set_status("Paused (tick %d)" % PlaybackManager.current_tick)
                else:
                    PlaybackManager.resume()
                    _set_status("Playing...")
            KEY_1: PlaybackManager.set_speed(0.5); _set_status("Speed: 0.5x")
            KEY_2: PlaybackManager.set_speed(1.0); _set_status("Speed: 1x")
            KEY_3: PlaybackManager.set_speed(2.0); _set_status("Speed: 2x")
            KEY_4: PlaybackManager.set_speed(4.0); _set_status("Speed: 4x")

## Base class for all AI blueprint nodes in the editor.

# Port type constants for GraphEdit type checking.

const PORT_COLORS := {
    PORT_FLOW: Color(0.9, 0.9, 0.9),   # white — execution flow
    PORT_BOOL: Color(0.3, 0.9, 0.3),   # green — condition result
}

# Node category colors for titlebar.
const CATEGORY_COLORS := {
    "flow":      Color(0.8, 0.5, 0.2),   # orange
    "condition": Color(0.3, 0.5, 0.8),   # blue
    "action":    Color(0.3, 0.7, 0.3),   # green
    "targeting": Color(0.8, 0.7, 0.2),   # yellow
}

var node_type: String = ""        # proto NodeType string, e.g. "NODE_PRIORITY_SELECTOR"
var node_category: String = ""    # "flow", "condition", "action", "targeting"
var node_params: Dictionary = {}  # parameter values (threshold, range, skill, tags, etc.)


func setup_blueprint_node(type: String, category: String, display_title: String) -> void:
    node_type = type
    node_category = category
    title = display_title


func get_param(key: String, default_val: Variant = "") -> Variant:
    return node_params.get(key, default_val)


func set_param(key: String, value: Variant) -> void:
    node_params[key] = value


func get_node_data() -> Dictionary:
    ## Returns serializable data for this node.
    return {
        "type": node_type,
        "category": node_category,
        "params": node_params.duplicate(),
        "position": {"x": position_offset.x, "y": position_offset.y},
    }


func load_node_data(data: Dictionary) -> void:
    ## Restores node state from serialized data.
    node_params = data.get("params", {}).duplicate()
    if "position" in data:
        position_offset = Vector2(data.position.x, data.position.y)
    _update_ui_from_params()

@onready var search_field: LineEdit = $VBox/SearchField

var _buttons_by_type: Dictionary = {}


func _ready() -> void:
    search_field.text_changed.connect(_on_search)
    _build_palette()


func _build_palette() -> void:
    # Create tabs by category.
    var categories := {"flow": "Flow", "condition": "Conditions", "targeting": "Targeting", "action": "Actions"}

    for cat_key: String in categories:
        var scroll := ScrollContainer.new()
        scroll.name = categories[cat_key]
        scroll.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
        var vbox := VBoxContainer.new()
        vbox.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
        scroll.add_child(vbox)
        tabs.add_child(scroll)

        for entry: Dictionary in NODE_CATALOG:
            if entry.category != cat_key:
                continue
            var btn := Button.new()
            btn.text = entry.label
            btn.tooltip_text = entry.desc
            btn.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
            btn.pressed.connect(_on_node_btn.bind(entry.type))
            vbox.add_child(btn)
            _buttons_by_type[entry.type] = btn


func _on_node_btn(node_type: String) -> void:
    node_requested.emit(node_type)


func _on_search(text: String) -> void:
    var query := text.to_lower()
    for entry: Dictionary in NODE_CATALOG:
        var btn: Button = _buttons_by_type.get(entry.type)
        if btn:
            btn.visible = query.is_empty() or entry.label.to_lower().contains(query)


func get_catalog_entry(node_type: String) -> Dictionary:
    for entry: Dictionary in NODE_CATALOG:
        if entry.type == node_type:
            return entry
    return {}

Step 2: Create blueprint_editor.gd

# roguelite/scripts/ui/blueprint_editor.gd
extends Control
## Blueprint Editor screen — visual AI tree builder using GraphEdit.

@onready var graph: GraphEdit = $HSplit/GraphEdit
@onready var palette: PanelContainer = $HSplit/Palette
@onready var back_btn: Button = $TopBar/BackButton
@onready var test_btn: Button = $TopBar/TestButton
@onready var clear_btn: Button = $TopBar/ClearButton
@onready var memory_label: Label = $BottomBar/MemoryLabel
@onready var node_count_label: Label = $BottomBar/NodeCountLabel

var _node_counter: int = 0

# Memory costs per node type (from GDD).
const MEMORY_COSTS := {
    "NODE_PRIORITY_SELECTOR": 2,
    "NODE_SEQUENCE": 1,
    "NODE_HP_BELOW": 1,
    "NODE_ENEMY_IN_RANGE": 2,
    "NODE_NEAREST_ENEMY": 1,
    "NODE_LOWEST_HP_ENEMY": 1,
    "NODE_MOVE_TO": 1,
    "NODE_USE_SKILL": 2,
    "NODE_WAIT": 1,
}


func _ready() -> void:
    UIManager.register_screen("blueprint_editor", self)

    graph.connection_request.connect(_on_connection_request)
    graph.disconnection_request.connect(_on_disconnection_request)
    graph.delete_nodes_request.connect(_on_delete_nodes_request)
    graph.right_disconnects = true

    palette.node_requested.connect(_on_add_node)
    back_btn.pressed.connect(func(): UIManager.go_back())
    test_btn.pressed.connect(_on_test)
    clear_btn.pressed.connect(_on_clear)

    _update_status()


func _on_connection_request(from_node: StringName, from_port: int,
                            to_node: StringName, to_port: int) -> void:
    # Prevent self-loops.
    if from_node == to_node:
        return
    # Prevent duplicate input connections.
    for con: Dictionary in graph.get_connection_list():
        if con.to_node == to_node and con.to_port == to_port:
            return
    graph.connect_node(from_node, from_port, to_node, to_port)


func _on_disconnection_request(from_node: StringName, from_port: int,
                                to_node: StringName, to_port: int) -> void:
    graph.disconnect_node(from_node, from_port, to_node, to_port)


func _on_delete_nodes_request(nodes: Array[StringName]) -> void:
    for node_name: StringName in nodes:
        var node := graph.get_node_or_null(NodePath(node_name))
        if node is BlueprintGraphNode:
            # Remove all connections to/from this node.
            for con: Dictionary in graph.get_connection_list():
                if con.from_node == node_name or con.to_node == node_name:
                    graph.disconnect_node(con.from_node, con.from_port,
                                          con.to_node, con.to_port)
            node.queue_free()
    await get_tree().process_frame
    _update_status()


func _on_add_node(node_type: String) -> void:
    var entry: Dictionary = palette.get_catalog_entry(node_type)
    if entry.is_empty():
        return

    _node_counter += 1
    var id := "node_%d" % _node_counter

    var gnode := BlueprintGraphNode.new()
    gnode.name = id
    gnode.setup_blueprint_node(node_type, entry.category, entry.label)
    gnode.position_offset = (graph.scroll_offset + Vector2(200, 150)) / graph.zoom

    # Add input port (slot 0 = input flow).
    var input_label := Label.new()
    input_label.text = "In"
    gnode.add_child(input_label)
    var has_input: bool = entry.get("ports_in", 0) > 0
    gnode.set_slot(0, has_input, BlueprintGraphNode.PORT_FLOW,
                   BlueprintGraphNode.PORT_COLORS[BlueprintGraphNode.PORT_FLOW],
                   false, 0, Color.WHITE)

    # Add parameter rows.
    var params: Array = entry.get("params", [])
    for i: int in params.size():
        var p: Dictionary = params[i]
        var row := HBoxContainer.new()
        var lbl := Label.new()
        lbl.text = p.label
        lbl.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
        row.add_child(lbl)

        match p.type:
            "float":
                var spin := SpinBox.new()
                spin.min_value = p.get("min", 0)
                spin.max_value = p.get("max", 999)
                spin.value = p.get("default", 0)
                spin.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
                spin.value_changed.connect(func(v: float): gnode.set_param(p.key, v))
                gnode.set_param(p.key, spin.value)
                row.add_child(spin)
            "string":
                var edit := LineEdit.new()
                edit.text = str(p.get("default", ""))
                edit.placeholder_text = p.label
                edit.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
                edit.text_changed.connect(func(t: String): gnode.set_param(p.key, t))
                gnode.set_param(p.key, edit.text)
                row.add_child(edit)

        gnode.add_child(row)
        gnode.set_slot(i + 1, false, 0, Color.WHITE, false, 0, Color.WHITE)

    # Add output ports (flow children slots).
    var out_count: int = entry.get("ports_out_flow", 0)
    var slot_offset: int = 1 + params.size()
    for j: int in out_count:
        var out_label := Label.new()
        out_label.text = "Child %d" % (j + 1) if out_count > 1 else "Out"
        out_label.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_RIGHT
        gnode.add_child(out_label)
        gnode.set_slot(slot_offset + j,
                       false, 0, Color.WHITE,
                       true, BlueprintGraphNode.PORT_FLOW,
                       BlueprintGraphNode.PORT_COLORS[BlueprintGraphNode.PORT_FLOW])

    graph.add_child(gnode)
    _update_status()


func _on_test() -> void:
    var build := serialize_to_build()
    if build.is_empty():
        return
    # Get profile screen and set the build.
    var profile_screen = UIManager._screens.get("profile")
    if profile_screen and profile_screen.has_method("set_build"):
        profile_screen.set_build(build)
    # Navigate to game view and start run.
    UIManager.navigate_to("game_view")
    await get_tree().process_frame
    var game_screen = UIManager._screens.get("game_view")
    if game_screen and game_screen.has_method("start_run"):
        game_screen.start_run(build)


func _on_clear() -> void:
    graph.clear_connections()
    for child in graph.get_children():
        if child is BlueprintGraphNode:
            child.queue_free()
    _node_counter = 0
    await get_tree().process_frame
    _update_status()


func _update_status() -> void:
    var total_cost: int = 0
    var count: int = 0
    for child in graph.get_children():
        if child is BlueprintGraphNode:
            count += 1
            total_cost += MEMORY_COSTS.get(child.node_type, 1)

    var max_memory: int = 20  # default, TODO: get from build
    memory_label.text = "Memory: %d / %d" % [total_cost, max_memory]
    node_count_label.text = "Nodes: %d" % count


func serialize_to_build() -> Dictionary:
    ## Convert the GraphEdit graph into a PlayerBuild Dictionary (protojson format).
    var connections := graph.get_connection_list()

    # Find root nodes (nodes with no incoming connections).
    var has_input: Dictionary = {}
    for con: Dictionary in connections:
        has_input[String(con.to_node)] = true

    var roots: Array[BlueprintGraphNode] = []
    for child in graph.get_children():
        if child is BlueprintGraphNode:
            if not has_input.has(child.name):
                roots.append(child)

    if roots.is_empty():
        push_warning("Blueprint has no root nodes!")
        return {}

    # Build tree from the first root (global AI).
    var global_ai := _serialize_node(roots[0], connections)

    # Get current profile stats/skills or use defaults.
    var profile_screen = UIManager._screens.get("profile")
    var current_build: Dictionary = {}
    if profile_screen and profile_screen.has_method("get_build"):
        current_build = profile_screen.get_build()

    return {
        "globalAi": global_ai,
        "totalMemory": current_build.get("totalMemory", 20),
        "globalMemory": current_build.get("globalMemory", 20),
        "skills": current_build.get("skills", [
            {
                "id": "basic_attack", "name": "Basic Attack",
                "damageMult": 1.0, "range": 40.0, "cooldownTicks": 15,
                "shape": "SHAPE_MELEE", "damageType": "DAMAGE_PHYSICAL",
                "tags": ["melee", "physical", "damage"]
            }
        ]),
        "stats": current_build.get("stats", {
            "maxHp": 100, "baseDamage": 15, "armor": 10.0,
            "resistance": 0.0, "speed": 3.0, "critChance": 0.05,
            "critMult": 1.5, "dodgeChance": 0.0,
            "blockChance": 0.0, "blockReduction": 0.0
        })
    }


func _serialize_node(gnode: BlueprintGraphNode, connections: Array) -> Dictionary:
    var result := {"type": gnode.node_type}

    # Add parameters if any.
    if not gnode.node_params.is_empty():
        var params := {}
        for key: String in gnode.node_params:
            var val = gnode.node_params[key]
            if val is float:
                params[key] = str(val)
            elif val is String and val != "":
                params[key] = val
        if not params.is_empty():
            result["parameters"] = params

    # Find children connected to this node's output ports.
    var children_by_port: Dictionary = {}
    for con: Dictionary in connections:
        if String(con.from_node) == gnode.name:
            var target_name := String(con.to_node)
            var target_node := graph.get_node_or_null(NodePath(target_name))
            if target_node is BlueprintGraphNode:
                children_by_port[con.from_port] = target_node

    if not children_by_port.is_empty():
        var sorted_ports := children_by_port.keys()
        sorted_ports.sort()
        var children_array := []
        for port: int in sorted_ports:
            children_array.append(_serialize_node(children_by_port[port], connections))
        result["children"] = children_array

    return result

    var btn_pressed := btn_normal.duplicate()

docs.title: Step 1: Isometric coordinate transform
docs.text:
File: roguelite/scripts/entities/character.gd

Add a static utility function and use it in apply_state():

# Standard 2:1 isometric projection
static func iso_transform(cart_x: float, cart_y: float) -> Vector2:
    return Vector2(
        (cart_x - cart_y) * 0.5,
        (cart_x + cart_y) * 0.25
    )

In apply_state(), replace:

position = Vector2(state.get("x", 0.0), state.get("y", 0.0))

With:

position = iso_transform(state.get("x", 0.0), state.get("y", 0.0))

docs.title: Step 4: Isometric floor rendering
docs.text:
File: roguelite/scripts/game_view.gd

Add a floor drawing function that renders a grid of diamond tiles for the room area. Use _draw() on a dedicated Node2D child, or create a simple script.

Option A — a _draw() override on a Floor node added to World:

# Floor draws diamond grid covering server room (0,0)→(1200,1000)
# Each tile is e.g. 64x64 in server space → diamond on screen
func _draw():
    var tile_size := 64.0
    var room_w := 1200.0
    var room_h := 1000.0
    for gx in range(0, int(room_w / tile_size)):
        for gy in range(0, int(room_h / tile_size)):
            var cx = (gx + 0.5) * tile_size
            var cy = (gy + 0.5) * tile_size
            var screen_pos = Character.iso_transform(cx, cy)
            var half_w = tile_size * 0.5 * 0.5
            var half_h = tile_size * 0.5 * 0.25
            var points = PackedVector2Array([
                screen_pos + Vector2(0, -half_h),
                screen_pos + Vector2(half_w, 0),
                screen_pos + Vector2(0, half_h),
                screen_pos + Vector2(-half_w, 0),
            ])
            draw_polygon(points, PackedColorArray([Color(0.15, 0.15, 0.2)]))
            draw_polyline(points + PackedVector2Array([points[0]]), Color(0.25, 0.25, 0.3), 1.0)

Place this Floor node BEFORE Entities in the World tree so it draws behind entities.

Test: Dark diamond grid visible as the arena floor.

Same approach — draw wall outlines along the 4 edges of the room in isometric projection.

The 4 corners of room (0,0), (1200,0), (1200,1000), (0,1000) projected through iso_transform form a diamond. Draw a thick outline around this diamond.

# In Floor _draw() after tile grid:
var corners = [
    Character.iso_transform(0, 0),
    Character.iso_transform(room_w, 0),
    Character.iso_transform(room_w, room_h),
    Character.iso_transform(0, room_h),
]
var wall_poly = PackedVector2Array(corners + [corners[0]])
draw_polyline(wall_poly, Color(0.5, 0.4, 0.3), 3.0)

docs.title: Sub-phase B: Floor Map + Navigation — Implementation Plan
Goal
docs.text: Add procedural floor map (graph of rooms), room-by-room navigation, and the full run loop: FloorMap → GameView → RoomResult → FloorMap → ... → Boss → NextFloor.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Player clicks Solo
  → Server creates Run (seed, floor=1)
  → Server generates FloorMap (graph)
  → Server sends SERVER_FLOOR_MAP
  → Client shows FloorMap screen

Player clicks room on map
  → Client sends CLIENT_SELECT_ROOM
  → Server validates selection
  → Combat room: simulate → SERVER_SIMULATION_RESULT
  → Client plays back → shows result
  → After victory: SERVER_FLOOR_MAP (updated, room marked cleared)
  → Client shows FloorMap again
  → ... repeat until Boss defeated
  → Boss victory: floor++ → new FloorMap

New package: server/internal/dungeon/

generator.go:

type Generator struct{}

func (g *Generator) Generate(floor, seed int) *pb.FloorMap

Algorithm: 1. Use math/rand with seed for determinism 2. Create layers 0 to N (N = 5 + floor/3, cap at 8) 3. Layer 0: single "start" node (not a room, just entry point) 4. Layer 1: always 1 Combat room 5. Middle layers: 1-3 rooms, types weighted (Combat 50%, Elite 15%, Treasure 15%, Shop 20%) 6. Last layer: always 1 Boss room 7. Connect: each node connects to 1-2 nodes in next layer. Ensure every node is reachable 8. Guarantee: at least 1 Shop and 1 Treasure on the floor 9. Set start node as current, layer-1 nodes as available

func RoomConfig(roomType pb.RoomType, floor int) SimConfig

Returns room size and enemy setup based on type: - Combat: 1200x1000, SpawnEnemies(floor) - Elite: 1400x1200, SpawnEliteEnemies(floor) - Boss: 1600x1400, SpawnBoss(floor) - Treasure/Shop: no simulation needed

docs.title: Sub-phase C: Treasure + Shop — Implementation Plan
Design: Minimal Viable Approach
docs.text:
Items are simple stat modifiers (e.g. +10 HP, +3 DMG, +5 ARM). No inventory management — picking/buying an item immediately applies the stat change to the player's build on the server side.

  • Treasure room: Server offers 3 random stat boost items, player picks 1, stats updated
  • Shop room: Server offers 4 items with gold prices, player buys 0+, stats updated per purchase
  • Gold: Earned after combat victories (amount based on room type: combat=10, elite=25, boss=50)
  • Persistent HP: Player HP carries between rooms (healed partially by some items)

docs.title: Step 1: Proto Changes
docs.text:
New opcodes:

CLIENT_TREASURE_PICK = 6;
CLIENT_SHOP_BUY = 7;
SERVER_TREASURE_OFFER = 14;
SERVER_SHOP_OFFER = 15;

New messages:

message StatModifier {
  string stat = 1;     // "maxHp", "baseDamage", "armor", "speed", "critChance", etc.
  float value = 2;     // +10, +3, +0.05, etc.
}

message RewardItem {
  string id = 1;
  string name = 2;
  string description = 3;
  repeated StatModifier modifiers = 4;
  int32 cost = 5;      // gold cost (shop only, 0 for treasure)
}

message TreasureOffer {
  repeated RewardItem items = 1;
}

message ShopOffer {
  repeated RewardItem items = 1;
  int32 player_gold = 2;
}

message TreasurePickRequest {
  string item_id = 1;
}

message ShopBuyRequest {
  string item_id = 1;
}

message ShopBuyResponse {
  bool success = 1;
  int32 remaining_gold = 2;
}

Modify SimulationResult: add int32 gold_earned = 7;

docs.title: 2D → 3D Migration Plan
docs.text:
For Claude: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

Goal: Replace the 2D isometric rendering with real 3D (orthogonal camera, GLB models, AnimationTree) while keeping the server and UI layers untouched.

Architecture: Server still outputs flat (x, y) coordinates. Client converts them to Vector3(x * SCALE, 0, y * SCALE) where SCALE = 0.01, giving a 12m x 10m room. Camera3D in orthogonal mode at iso angle (-35° X, -45° Y) reproduces the same Diablo/PoE feel. All UI (Control-based screens) remains 2D.

Tech Stack: Godot 4.6, GDScript, GLB models (KayKit Adventurers CC0), AnimationTree + AnimationNodeStateMachine.

Character3D (Node3D)                  ← root, script: character_3d.gd
├── Model (Node3D)                    ← rotation pivot for facing direction
│   └── <imported GLB scene>          ← swapped per entity type in setup()

transform = Transform3D(1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 2.2, 0)
billboard = 1

docs.title: Task 3: Create character_3d.gd Script
docs.text:
Files: - Create: roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd

This is the main script. It replaces character.gd entirely. Key differences: - Positions are Vector3 (converted from server x, y) - Model rotation replaces sprite direction rows - GLB models loaded per entity type instead of sprite sheets

Step 1: Write the script

extends Node3D
## 3D visual representation of a simulation entity.
## No physics — position set directly from server snapshots.

@onready var model_pivot: Node3D = $Model
@onready var name_label: Label3D = $NameLabel
@onready var hp_bar: Label3D = $HPBar
@onready var ai_debug_label: Label3D = $AIDebugLabel

var entity_id: String = ""
var entity_type: int = 0

## Server (x, y) → Godot Vector3(x, 0, y) scale factor.
## Server room is 1200x1000 units → 12m x 10m in 3D.
const SCALE := 0.01

var _prev_server_x: float = 0.0
var _prev_server_y: float = 0.0
var _target_rotation_y: float = 0.0
var _current_action: int = 0

# Model scenes — preloaded per entity type.
# Adjust paths after importing GLB files.
var _model_scene_player: PackedScene = preload("res://assets/models/kaykit/Barbarian.glb")
var _model_scene_melee: PackedScene = preload("res://assets/models/kaykit/Skeleton.glb")
var _model_scene_ranged: PackedScene = preload("res://assets/models/kaykit/SkeletonMage.glb")

# Protojson enum string -> int mappings (same as character.gd).
const ACTION_MAP := {
    "ACTION_IDLE": 0, "ACTION_MOVE": 1, "ACTION_ATTACK": 2,
    "ACTION_HIT": 3, "ACTION_DEAD": 4, "ACTION_CAST": 5,
}

const NODE_DISPLAY_NAMES := {
    "NODE_UNSPECIFIED": "?",
    "NODE_PRIORITY_SELECTOR": "Priority",
    "NODE_SEQUENCE": "Sequence",
    "NODE_HP_CHECK": "HPCheck",
    "NODE_DISTANCE_CHECK": "DistCheck",
    "NODE_MOVE_TO": "MoveTo",
    "NODE_FLEE_FROM": "Flee",
    "NODE_USE_SKILL": "UseSkill",
    "NODE_WAIT": "Wait",
}


static func parse_action(raw) -> int:
    if raw is int or raw is float:
        return int(raw)
    return ACTION_MAP.get(str(raw), 0)


static func server_to_world(sx: float, sy: float) -> Vector3:
    ## Convert server (x, y) to Godot 3D world position.
    return Vector3(sx * SCALE, 0.0, sy * SCALE)


func setup(id: String, type_val: int, display_name: String = "") -> void:
    entity_id = id
    entity_type = type_val
    name_label.text = display_name if display_name != "" else id

    # Clear any previous model.
    for child in model_pivot.get_children():
        child.queue_free()

    match type_val:
        1:  # PLAYER
            _instantiate_model(_model_scene_player)
        2:  # ENEMY_MELEE
            _instantiate_model(_model_scene_melee)
        3:  # ENEMY_RANGED
            _instantiate_model(_model_scene_ranged)
        4:  # PROJECTILE
            _setup_projectile()
            return
        _:
            _instantiate_model(_model_scene_player)


func _instantiate_model(scene: PackedScene) -> void:
    var instance := scene.instantiate()
    model_pivot.add_child(instance)
    # KayKit models may need scale adjustment — tweak after visual test.
    # instance.scale = Vector3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)


func _setup_projectile() -> void:
    ## Simple sphere for projectiles.
    var mesh_inst := MeshInstance3D.new()
    var sphere := SphereMesh.new()
    sphere.radius = 0.15
    sphere.height = 0.3
    mesh_inst.mesh = sphere
    var mat := StandardMaterial3D.new()
    mat.albedo_color = Color.YELLOW
    mat.emission_enabled = true
    mat.emission = Color.YELLOW
    mat.emission_energy_multiplier = 2.0
    mesh_inst.material_override = mat
    model_pivot.add_child(mesh_inst)
    # Elevate projectile to waist height.
    mesh_inst.position.y = 0.8
    name_label.visible = false
    hp_bar.visible = false


func apply_state(state: Dictionary) -> void:
    var sx: float = state.get("x", 0.0)
    var sy: float = state.get("y", 0.0)
    var world_pos := server_to_world(sx, sy)
    position = world_pos

    # Projectiles: just position, no rotation/HP.
    if entity_type == 4:
        return

    # Rotation from movement delta.
    var dx: float = sx - _prev_server_x
    var dy: float = sy - _prev_server_y
    if absf(dx) > 0.5 or absf(dy) > 0.5:
        _target_rotation_y = atan2(dx, dy)
    _prev_server_x = sx
    _prev_server_y = sy

    # Smooth rotation.
    model_pivot.rotation.y = lerp_angle(model_pivot.rotation.y, _target_rotation_y, 0.3)

    # HP bar (text-based for now).
    var hp: float = state.get("health", 0)
    var max_hp: float = state.get("maxHealth", 1)
    var ratio: float = hp / max_hp if max_hp > 0 else 0.0
    var filled: int = int(ratio * 10)
    hp_bar.text = "█".repeat(filled) + "░".repeat(10 - filled)
    hp_bar.modulate = Color(
        lerpf(0.8, 0.2, ratio),  # red when low
        lerpf(0.2, 0.8, ratio),  # green when high
        0.2, 0.9
    )
    hp_bar.visible = hp > 0

    # Action feedback.
    var action: int = parse_action(state.get("action", 0))
    _update_visuals(action)
    _current_action = action

    # AI debug overlay.
    _update_ai_debug(state)


func _update_visuals(action: int) -> void:
    ## Visual feedback per action. Phase A: simple modulate.
    ## Phase B replaces this with AnimationTree state machine.
    match action:
        4:  # ACTION_DEAD
            _set_model_modulate(Color(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
            hp_bar.visible = false
        2, 5:  # ACTION_ATTACK, ACTION_CAST
            _set_model_modulate(Color(1.2, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0))
        3:  # ACTION_HIT
            _set_model_modulate(Color(1.0, 0.5, 0.5, 1.0))
        _:  # IDLE, MOVE
            _set_model_modulate(Color(1, 1, 1, 1))


func _set_model_modulate(color: Color) -> void:
    ## Apply color tint to all MeshInstance3D children.
    ## Simple approach — finds meshes recursively in model.
    for mesh in _find_meshes(model_pivot):
        mesh.modulate = color  # Label3D/Sprite3D
        # For MeshInstance3D, use material override:
        if mesh is MeshInstance3D:
            var mat := mesh.get_active_material(0)
            if mat is StandardMaterial3D:
                mat.albedo_color = color


func _find_meshes(node: Node) -> Array:
    var result: Array = []
    if node is MeshInstance3D:
        result.append(node)
    for child in node.get_children():
        result.append_array(_find_meshes(child))
    return result


func _update_ai_debug(state: Dictionary) -> void:
    if entity_type != 1 or not SettingsManager.show_ai_decisions:
        ai_debug_label.visible = false
        return

    var module_name: String = state.get("activeModule", "")
    var node_type: String = state.get("activeNode", "")
    var skill: String = state.get("activeSkill", "")
    var node_short: String = NODE_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(node_type, node_type)

    var parts: PackedStringArray = []
    if module_name != "":
        parts.append(module_name)
    if skill != "":
        parts.append(node_short + ": " + skill)
    elif node_short != "":
        parts.append(node_short)

    if parts.is_empty():
        ai_debug_label.visible = false
        return

    ai_debug_label.text = " | ".join(parts)
    ai_debug_label.visible = true

Step 2: Verify script compiles

Open Godot editor — no parse errors in the Output panel.

Step 3: Commit

git add roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd
git commit -m "feat: add character_3d.gd with server-to-3D coordinate mapping"

docs.title: Task 4: Create game_world_3d Scene (Environment, Camera, Light, Floor)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: roguelite/scenes/game/game_world_3d.tscn - Create: roguelite/scripts/game/game_world_3d.gd

This replaces the old World (Node2D) + Floor (Node2D/iso_floor.gd) + Camera2D + Entities (Node2D) inside the SubViewport.

Step 1: Create the scene

Scene tree:

GameWorld3D (Node3D)                  ← script: game_world_3d.gd
├── Camera3D                          ← orthogonal, iso angle
├── DirectionalLight3D                ← sun-like, soft shadows
├── WorldEnvironment                  ← ambient light, tone mapping
├── Floor (MeshInstance3D)            ← PlaneMesh 12m x 10m
├── Walls (Node3D)                    ← optional boundary indicators
└── Entities (Node3D)                 ← characters spawned here

Key properties:

Camera3D:

projection = PROJECTION_ORTHOGONAL
size = 15.0                          # visible area in meters
rotation_degrees = Vector3(-35, -45, 0)
position = Vector3(10, 12, 10)       # initial offset (adjusted by follow logic)
near = 0.1
far = 100.0

DirectionalLight3D:

rotation_degrees = Vector3(-50, -30, 0)
shadow_enabled = true
light_energy = 1.2
shadow_bias = 0.05

WorldEnvironment → Environment:

ambient_light_source = COLOR
ambient_light_color = Color(0.3, 0.3, 0.35)
ambient_light_energy = 0.5
tonemap_mode = TONE_MAP_ACES

Floor (MeshInstance3D + PlaneMesh):

PlaneMesh.size = Vector2(12, 10)     # matches ROOM_W * SCALE, ROOM_H * SCALE
position = Vector3(6, 0, 5)          # centered (room goes 0..12 x 0..10)

Floor material:

StandardMaterial3D:
  albedo_color = Color(0.2, 0.2, 0.25)
  roughness = 0.9

Optional grid overlay: a second PlaneMesh slightly above with a tiling grid texture, or a shader that draws grid lines.

Step 2: Write game_world_3d.gd

extends Node3D
## 3D game world — camera follow, zoom, environment.

@onready var camera: Camera3D = $Camera3D
@onready var entities_node: Node3D = $Entities

## Camera offset from target in world space.
## Computed from the iso angle so camera orbits correctly.
var _camera_offset: Vector3
var _camera_target: Vector3 = Vector3(6, 0, 5)  # room center default
var _camera_free: bool = false
var _camera_drag: bool = false
var _last_mouse_pos: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO

const CAMERA_SMOOTH_SPEED := 5.0
const ZOOM_STEP := 0.5
const ZOOM_MIN := 8.0
const ZOOM_MAX := 30.0


func _ready() -> void:
    # Store initial offset so we can reposition camera relative to target.
    _camera_offset = camera.position - _camera_target


func _process(delta: float) -> void:
    if _camera_free:
        return
    # Smooth follow.
    var desired := _camera_target + _camera_offset
    camera.position = camera.position.lerp(desired, delta * CAMERA_SMOOTH_SPEED)


func follow_target(world_pos: Vector3) -> void:
    ## Called each tick to update camera target (e.g. player position).
    if not _camera_free:
        _camera_target = world_pos


func set_free_mode(free: bool) -> void:
    _camera_free = free


func zoom_in() -> void:
    camera.size = clampf(camera.size - ZOOM_STEP, ZOOM_MIN, ZOOM_MAX)


func zoom_out() -> void:
    camera.size = clampf(camera.size + ZOOM_STEP, ZOOM_MIN, ZOOM_MAX)


func snap_to_target() -> void:
    _camera_free = false
    camera.position = _camera_target + _camera_offset

Step 3: Commit

git add roguelite/scenes/game/game_world_3d.tscn roguelite/scripts/game/game_world_3d.gd
git commit -m "feat: add 3D game world scene with ortho camera, light, floor"

In the .tscn file, the changes are: 1. Remove ext_resource for iso_floor.gd (id="2_floor") 2. Remove all nodes under SubViewportContainer/SubViewport (World, Floor, Camera2D, Entities) 3. Add instance of game_world_3d.tscn as child of SubViewport

+[ext_resource type="PackedScene" path="res://scenes/game/game_world_3d.tscn" id="2_world3d"]

-

-script = ExtResource("2_floor")

-[node name="Camera2D" type="Camera2D" parent="SubViewportContainer/SubViewport/World"]

-
-[node name="Entities" type="Node2D" parent="SubViewportContainer/SubViewport/World"]
-y_sort_enabled = true
+[node name="GameWorld3D" parent="SubViewportContainer/SubViewport" instance=ExtResource("2_world3d")]

Step 2: Update game_view.gd

Change references from 2D to 3D:

# OLD:
const CharacterScene := preload("res://scenes/entities/character.tscn")
@onready var entities_node: Node2D = $SubViewportContainer/SubViewport/World/Entities
@onready var camera: Camera2D = $SubViewportContainer/SubViewport/World/Camera2D

# NEW:
const CharacterScene := preload("res://scenes/entities/character_3d.tscn")
@onready var world_3d: Node3D = $SubViewportContainer/SubViewport/GameWorld3D
@onready var entities_node: Node3D = $SubViewportContainer/SubViewport/GameWorld3D/Entities

Remove the camera direct reference — camera control goes through world_3d.

Update _on_playback_tick:

# OLD camera follow:
if not _camera_free:
    for eid: String in _entities:
        var ent: Node2D = _entities[eid]
        if ent.entity_type == 1:
            camera.position = ent.position
            break

# NEW camera follow:
if not _camera_free:
    for eid: String in _entities:
        var ent: Node3D = _entities[eid]
        if ent.entity_type == 1:
            world_3d.follow_target(ent.position)
            break

Update _spawn_entities:

# OLD:
var character: Node2D = CharacterScene.instantiate()

# NEW:
var character: Node3D = CharacterScene.instantiate()

Update camera input handling in _unhandled_input:

# OLD zoom:
camera.zoom = (camera.zoom * 1.1).clamp(...)

# NEW zoom:
elif event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP:
    world_3d.zoom_in()
elif event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN:
    world_3d.zoom_out()

# OLD pan:
camera.position -= event.relative / camera.zoom

# NEW pan (project mouse delta onto 3D ground plane):
# Simple version — move camera offset by scaled mouse delta:
var pan_speed := 0.05
world_3d.camera.position += Vector3(-event.relative.x, 0, -event.relative.y) * pan_speed

# HOME key:
world_3d.snap_to_target()

Also update _camera_free references to go through world_3d.set_free_mode().

Step 3: Test

Run: cd server && go run ./cmd/server in one terminal. Run the game in Godot. Go to Solo run. Expected: entities render in 3D, camera follows player, playback works.

Step 4: Commit

git add roguelite/scenes/game/game_view.tscn roguelite/scripts/game_view.gd
git commit -m "feat: integrate 3D world into game_view, replace 2D SubViewport"

func _setup_projectile() -> void:

    var particles := GPUParticles3D.new()
    var mat := ParticleProcessMaterial.new()
    mat.emission_shape = ParticleProcessMaterial.EMISSION_SHAPE_POINT

docs.title: Phase B: AnimationTree (Smooth Animations)
docs.text: Replaces the simple color-tint feedback from Phase A with proper skeletal animations driven by AnimationTree state machine.

docs.title: Task 9: Set Up AnimationTree with StateMachine
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: roguelite/scenes/entities/character_3d.tscn - Modify: roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd

Step 1: Understand KayKit animation structure

KayKit GLB files embed an AnimationPlayer with named animations. After import, check what names exist:

# In Godot editor: click the GLB, look at the Animation panel.
# Expected names (KayKit Adventurers):
# Idle, Walk, Run, Attack1, Attack2, Death, HitRecieve, etc.
# Exact names vary — verify in editor before coding.

Step 2: Add AnimationTree to character_3d.tscn

Add as sibling of Model node:

Character3D (Node3D)
├── Model (Node3D)
│   └── <GLB instance with AnimationPlayer>
├── AnimationTree                     ← NEW
├── NameLabel (Label3D)
├── HPBar (Label3D)
└── AIDebugLabel (Label3D)

AnimationTree properties:

tree_root = AnimationNodeStateMachine (created in Step 3)
anim_player = path to the AnimationPlayer inside the GLB instance
active = true

Step 3: Build the state machine

Create the AnimationNodeStateMachine programmatically in _ready() or via scene setup:

StateMachine:
├── Idle         → AnimationNodeAnimation("Idle")
├── Locomotion   → AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D (see Task 10)
├── Attack       → AnimationNodeAnimation("Attack1")
├── Death        → AnimationNodeAnimation("Death")
└── Hit          → AnimationNodeAnimation("HitRecieve")

Transitions:
- Idle → Locomotion:  advance_condition = "is_moving"
- Locomotion → Idle:  advance_condition = "is_idle"
- * → Attack:         advance_condition = "is_attacking", switch_mode = AT_END
- * → Death:          advance_condition = "is_dead", switch_mode = IMMEDIATE
- * → Hit:            advance_condition = "is_hit", switch_mode = IMMEDIATE
- Attack → Idle:      auto_advance = true (after animation ends)
- Hit → Idle:         auto_advance = true (after animation ends)

In GDScript (inside _ready() or a setup method, after model is instantiated):

func _setup_animation_tree() -> void:
    # Find AnimationPlayer in the instantiated GLB model.
    var anim_player: AnimationPlayer = _find_child_of_type(model_pivot, "AnimationPlayer")
    if not anim_player:
        push_warning("No AnimationPlayer found in model for %s" % entity_id)
        return

    var anim_tree := AnimationTree.new()
    add_child(anim_tree)
    anim_tree.anim_player = anim_tree.get_path_to(anim_player)

    var sm := AnimationNodeStateMachine.new()

    # Add states.
    var idle_node := AnimationNodeAnimation.new()
    idle_node.animation = &"Idle"  # Verify exact name from GLB
    sm.add_node(&"Idle", idle_node, Vector2(0, 0))

    var attack_node := AnimationNodeAnimation.new()
    attack_node.animation = &"Attack1"
    sm.add_node(&"Attack", attack_node, Vector2(200, 0))

    var death_node := AnimationNodeAnimation.new()
    death_node.animation = &"Death"
    sm.add_node(&"Death", death_node, Vector2(200, 200))

    var hit_node := AnimationNodeAnimation.new()
    hit_node.animation = &"HitRecieve"
    sm.add_node(&"Hit", hit_node, Vector2(0, 200))

    # Locomotion — simple animation for now, BlendSpace2D in Task 10.
    var walk_node := AnimationNodeAnimation.new()
    walk_node.animation = &"Walk"
    sm.add_node(&"Locomotion", walk_node, Vector2(-200, 0))

    # Transitions.
    _add_transition(sm, &"Idle", &"Locomotion", "is_moving")
    _add_transition(sm, &"Locomotion", &"Idle", "is_idle")
    _add_transition(sm, &"Idle", &"Attack", "is_attacking")
    _add_transition(sm, &"Locomotion", &"Attack", "is_attacking")
    _add_transition(sm, &"Idle", &"Death", "is_dead")
    _add_transition(sm, &"Locomotion", &"Death", "is_dead")

    # Attack → Idle: auto-advance after animation finishes.
    var t_attack_idle := AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.new()
    t_attack_idle.advance_mode = AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.ADVANCE_MODE_AUTO
    sm.add_transition(&"Attack", &"Idle", t_attack_idle)

    # Hit → Idle: auto-advance.
    var t_hit_idle := AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.new()
    t_hit_idle.advance_mode = AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.ADVANCE_MODE_AUTO
    sm.add_transition(&"Hit", &"Idle", t_hit_idle)

    anim_tree.tree_root = sm
    anim_tree.active = true
    _anim_tree = anim_tree


func _add_transition(sm: AnimationNodeStateMachine, from: StringName, to: StringName, condition: String) -> void:
    var t := AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.new()
    t.advance_condition = condition
    sm.add_transition(from, to, t)

Step 4: Commit

git add roguelite/scenes/entities/character_3d.tscn roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd
git commit -m "feat: add AnimationTree state machine to character_3d"

docs.title: Task 10: BlendSpace2D for Locomotion (8 Directions)
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd

Step 1: Replace simple Walk node with BlendSpace2D

The BlendSpace2D blends between directional walk/run animations based on a 2D vector (direction_x, direction_y).

# In _setup_animation_tree(), replace the simple walk_node with:

var blend_space := AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.new()
blend_space.blend_mode = AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.BLEND_MODE_DISCRETE

# 8 directional points on the unit circle.
# If KayKit only has Walk/Run (no directional variants), use the same
# animation for all points — the model rotation handles facing.
var walk_anim := AnimationNodeAnimation.new()
walk_anim.animation = &"Walk"

# For a single walk animation, just add one center point.
# When directional anims become available, add 8 points.
blend_space.add_blend_point(walk_anim, Vector2(0, 0))

sm.add_node(&"Locomotion", blend_space, Vector2(-200, 0))

Note: KayKit Adventurers likely has a single "Walk" animation (the 3D model rotates to face direction). True 8-directional blending is only needed for sprite-based or motion-matched setups. For now, keep it simple — one Walk anim, model rotation handles direction. Upgrade to BlendSpace2D with Run/Walk speed blending later.

Step 2: Update apply_state to set blend position

# In apply_state(), after calculating direction:
if _anim_tree:
    var normalized_dir := Vector2(dx, dy).normalized()
    _anim_tree.set("parameters/Locomotion/blend_position", normalized_dir)

Step 3: Test

Run a simulation. Verify: - Character walks with Walk animation - Model rotates to face movement direction - Smooth transition between Idle ↔ Walk

Step 4: Commit

git add roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd
git commit -m "feat: add BlendSpace2D locomotion with directional blending"

docs.title: Task 11: Connect AnimationTree to apply_state Playback
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd

Step 1: Replace _update_visuals with AnimationTree parameters

Replace the color-tint based _update_visuals() with animation state transitions:

func _update_visuals(action: int) -> void:
    if not _anim_tree:
        return

    # Reset all conditions.
    _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_moving", false)
    _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_idle", false)
    _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_attacking", false)
    _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_dead", false)
    _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_hit", false)

    match action:
        0:  # ACTION_IDLE
            _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_idle", true)
        1:  # ACTION_MOVE
            _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_moving", true)
        2, 5:  # ACTION_ATTACK, ACTION_CAST
            _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_attacking", true)
        3:  # ACTION_HIT
            _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_hit", true)
        4:  # ACTION_DEAD
            _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_dead", true)
            hp_bar.visible = false

Step 2: Handle death persistence

Death should be a final state — once dead, don't transition back:

var _is_dead: bool = false

func _update_visuals(action: int) -> void:
    if not _anim_tree or _is_dead:
        return

    if action == 4:  # ACTION_DEAD
        _is_dead = true
        _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_dead", true)
        hp_bar.visible = false
        return

    # ... rest of conditions ...

Step 3: Test full playback loop

  1. Start simulation with combat
  2. Verify: Idle animation plays when entity stands still
  3. Verify: Walk animation plays during movement
  4. Verify: Attack animation triggers on attack action, returns to idle
  5. Verify: Death animation plays once and stays
  6. Verify: No animation glitches between ticks (smooth transitions)

Step 4: Commit

git add roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd
git commit -m "feat: drive AnimationTree from apply_state playback actions"

docs.title: Task 12: Polish Transitions and Timing
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd

Step 1: Tune transition durations

# In _add_transition(), add crossfade:
func _add_transition(sm, from, to, condition) -> void:
    var t := AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.new()
    t.advance_condition = condition
    t.xfade_time = 0.15  # 150ms crossfade for smooth blending
    sm.add_transition(from, to, t)

Step 2: Handle attack one-shot timing

The server sends ACTION_ATTACK for a few ticks, then returns to ACTION_IDLE. If the attack animation is longer than those ticks, the state machine might cut it short. Solutions:

# Option A: Let attack play fully (auto-advance to Idle handles this).
# Only set is_attacking on the FIRST tick of an attack sequence.
var _attack_started: bool = false

func _update_visuals(action: int) -> void:
    # ...
    match action:
        2, 5:
            if not _attack_started:
                _anim_tree.set("parameters/conditions/is_attacking", true)
                _attack_started = true
        _:
            _attack_started = false
    # ...

Step 3: Adjust model scale

KayKit models may be too large or too small relative to the 12m x 10m room. Adjust in _instantiate_model():

func _instantiate_model(scene: PackedScene) -> void:
    var instance := scene.instantiate()
    model_pivot.add_child(instance)
    # Typical KayKit models are ~1 unit tall. Adjust if needed:
    # instance.scale = Vector3(1.5, 1.5, 1.5)

Test with the room — entities should be clearly visible but not take up too much of the floor.

Step 4: Final visual pass

  • Adjust Label3D positions (NameLabel, HPBar, AIDebugLabel) to float above the 3D model
  • Adjust font sizes for readability at the camera distance
  • Ensure projectile height matches character waist

Step 5: Commit

git add roguelite/scripts/entities/character_3d.gd
git commit -m "polish: tune animation transitions, model scale, label positions"

docs.title: Reference: Server Coordinate Mapping
docs.text:
The server operates in 2D (x, y) space with room size 1200 x 1000. The conversion:

Server (x=0..1200, y=0..1000)
    ↓  × 0.01
Godot 3D (x=0..12, y=0, z=0..10)

Camera is orthogonal at iso angle — rotation_degrees = (-35, -45, 0). This means: - Moving right on server (+x) moves right-and-toward-camera in 3D - Moving down on server (+y) moves left-and-toward-camera in 3D - Combined effect = classic isometric diamond view

Model rotation uses atan2(dx, dz) where dx and dz are server deltas scaled to 3D. The model faces the direction of movement.
